authoredFrom: Erlang call semantics + the pinned grammar's remote/internal_fun/external_fun shapes, before this fixture's F3 run. `?MODULE:m()` is the idiomatic self-dispatch and the module IS known, so it resolves exactly like a module-qualified call while the `?MODULE` use itself still emits its macro reference. A fun value keeps its module qualification and is a REFERENCE, never a call. A dynamic remote (`M:dyn(1)`, `erlang:F(2)`) has no statically nameable callee: naming the bare leaf would conflate every module's `dyn`/`F`, so nothing is emitted (ER-D23).

expectRelationships.note: the remote callee LEAF's line, module-qualified per ER-D1
the ?MODULE expansion: the module is this file's, so the call resolves exactly like a qualified one
the ?MODULE use itself is still a macro reference

forbidRelationships.note: ER-D23: a dynamic remote names no callee; the bare leaf would conflate every module's dyn/1
?MODULE:m() keeps the module - a bare m would conflate every module's m/0
